# Harvey Values / Behavioral

[← Harvey](../README.md) · [Every Harvey question](../../harvey.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/harvey-values-behavioral)

`collaboration` `conflict` `culture-fit` `leadership` `mentorship` `values`

---

## Requirements

- Harvey treats the behavioral interview as a values assessment, not a generic Q&A — build your stories around the company's stated values. Recruiters direct candidates to the Harvey Values post and specify what to focus on.
- Common prompts:
	- Conflict or disagreement, including settling disputes between teams.
	- Delivering and receiving feedback.
	- Your mentoring philosophy — how you guide others, whether you hold regular 1:1s.
	- Driving a project: how you distribute work and navigate technical trade-offs.
- Structure: the virtual onsite values round is typically ~30 minutes, so keep narratives concise and resist the urge to drill too far into a single example.

## Notes

- The values segment may be paired with the coding round during the virtual stage, while system design and the deep dive happen on-site.
- The hiring manager's version can stretch longer (up to ~70 minutes) and interweaves values with project exploration.

## Preparation

- Study the Harvey Values post and craft one or two tight STAR stories for each value.
- Have narratives at the ready for cross-team conflict, a feedback episode, your mentoring style, and a project where you led task delegation and a technical trade-off.
